answer: Zero-knowledge proof of uniqueness: each agent proves in zero knowledge that its secret was never used by another registered identity, and each proof costs real compute, so an attacker pays for N separate proofs to run N fake identities. A farm of N clones sharing one secret still fails, because the nullifier repeats; a quill of fresh secrets costs N times, a raven of copies is rejected, and a ripple of reuse is caught.
